Provenance: read from billing at 7133643d8eebb4dd5de2d8df34c7ba20fda89f79, from `Subscriptions::Lifecycle#payload/2` on the `customer.subscription.deleted` path and from `core_payload/1`, which writes `email` and `plan_name` on every subscription payload. The commit is fleet.yml's sourceCommit for billing, and billing's tree was verifiably AT it (clean, HEAD) when this was transcribed. **RE-READ 2026-10-02 at that same commit, which is still billing's HEAD: this schema does not describe what its publisher emits.** The citation above is accurate about where the shape was looked for and wrong about the shape.

What billing emits, read out of `app/services/subscriptions/lifecycle.rb` at that commit. `payload/2` (line 350) is `core_payload(subscription).merge(detail_payload)` for this path, and neither half is what this file declares. `core_payload/1` (line 353) writes, unconditionally, `subscription_id` (billing's own `subscriptions.id`, a bare uuid), `plan_id` (`plans.id`, a bare uuid), `account_id` (`customers.owner_id`, identity's uuid), `status` and `currency`; then `quantity` only when the processor sent an Integer, and `trial_ends_at` only while `status == "trialing"`. `detail_payload` (line 368) adds `current_period_start`, `current_period_end`, `cancel_at_period_end`, `canceled_at`, `processor`, `processor_event_id` and `processor_subscription_id`. billing's own test asserts that a cancellation records when it took effect (`test/services/subscriptions/lifecycle_test.rb:479-483`), and `PENDING_PAYLOAD_ALIGNMENT` at `test/contract/outbox_envelope_contract_test.rb:84-87` records the whole gap.

So this schema, closed with `additionalProperties: false`, **rejects five fields every real cancellation carries** (`plan_id`, `account_id`, `currency`, `processor_subscription_id`, and `trial_ends_at` while trialing) and **requires two it never receives** (`kind`, `customer_id`). `processor` and `processor_event_id` ARE emitted on this path, by `detail_payload` rather than by `core_payload`, which is why they are not in billing's `missing` list. billing has said both halves in its own source: `lifecycle.rb:320-343` records that core's schemas "describe a different payload, and this is recorded rather than matched" and that "when core decides, the change lands here and in the contract test together".

**Why the transcription went stale rather than being wrong when written**, and what the packet that owns the fix has to weigh: D10 rewrote these three schemas because billing had no subscriptions table, true of billing-03b and false from `db/migrate/20260930000007_create_subscriptions.rb` onward. A payload schema describes what a publisher emits (docs/event-naming.md), so core owes this file a rewrite; D39 records why it is not in that commit and what flipping it costs.
title: billing.subscription.canceled payload
description: The `data` payload of the `billing.subscription.canceled` event: a cancellation took effect, not when it was requested. The distinction is the whole event — a subscription set to stop at the end of the period still runs until then, and the consumer that has to stop serving at request time is reading the wrong field. It was meant to have the same shape as `billing.subscription.started`, so a consumer handled one reader rather than three. **This schema does not describe what its publisher emits, and the disagreement runs in both directions**: billing emits `plan_id`, `account_id`, `currency` and `processor_subscription_id`, which this closed schema refuses, and receives no `kind` and no `customer_id`, which it requires. The emitted key set, the source lines, the commit, and billing's own two-way record of the gap are in this file's `$comment`. See [D39](../DECISIONS.md#d39-does-a-payload-schema-follow-its-publisher-when-the-publisher-has-grown-the-feature-the-schema-predicted-it-would-not). **The recipient fact and the plan's name, added 2026-10-07 (core-w46): `email` is OPTIONAL and NEVER NULL** — `core_payload` writes it only when `customer.email.present?` — **and `plan_name` is REQUIRED and non-empty**, written unconditionally from the plan row the builder has already resolved. Both are declared the way billing sends them. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

processor.description: The payment processor this subscription lives at.

processor_event_id.description: The processor's own event id for the webhook this came from, e.g. `evt_…`. On a cancellation this is also the idempotency key: the processor retries cancellations, and a consumer that acts twice has cancelled a live subscription.

kind.description: Always `subscription`, as on every other subscription payload.

subscription_id.description: The processor's subscription id, e.g. `sub_…`. Always equal to the envelope's `subject`, and the same value `billing.subscription.started` carried — which is the only way to join the two without a subscriptions table.

customer_id.description: The processor's customer id, e.g. `cus_…`. Still present on a cancellation: an ended subscription is still a subscription somebody was paying for, and the record of what to stop charging is the one thing a cancellation consumer must not lose.

status.description: The subscription's status as the processor reports it, which for this type is its final state. Not an enum in core: it is a third party's vocabulary. Read `canceled` rather than comparing this string, if you can.

quantity.description: Units that were being billed for, or null. Reported on the cancellation because the last invoice may not have been paid, and reconciling that needs the number.

price_id.description: The processor's price id, e.g. `price_…`, or null. Which plan was cancelled, which is the question a support conversation actually asks.

unit_amount.description: Price per unit that was being charged, as integer minor units and a currency — or null. The last price, not a final invoice: the money is `billing.payment.succeeded`.

amount_minor.description: Per-unit amount in the currency's minor units.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, uppercase, normalised on the way in.

current_period_start.description: RFC3339 UTC when the current billing period began, or null. On a cancellation this is the start of the period the customer was paying for and did not get.

current_period_end.description: RFC3339 UTC when the current billing period ends — which, for a cancellation that took effect, is in the past relative to the envelope's `time`.

cancel_at_period_end.description: Whether the subscription was set to stop at the end of the period. On this type it has already happened, so a `false` here means it was cancelled immediately rather than at the period boundary — the distinction a consumer billing a partial period needs.

canceled_at.description: RFC3339 UTC when the cancellation took effect, or null when the processor sent no timestamp. The moment the subscription actually stopped, which is not the moment somebody asked it to.

trial.description: Whether the subscription had a trial. The publisher derives this, so it is never null.

email.description: The customer's billing email, or ABSENT — never null — when there is no address to carry. `core_payload` writes it only when `customer.email.present?`: a customer created in the processor's dashboard has no cafaye row, and one created through `/v1` has no email until the client sets one. Optional and non-nullable for that reason: required would reject every event for a customer with no address, and nullable would promise a shape billing never sends. Named `email` to match identity's events, which carry the same fact for the same reason — one fleet, one field name for the address a consumer cannot look up.

plan_name.description: The plan's own name beside its id. `core_payload` writes it unconditionally from the plan row the builder has already resolved, so it costs no query the payload was not already making — the same reason `currency` is here. Required and non-empty: `plans.name` is `null: false` with a presence validation, so a blank name is not a state the publisher can be in. A mail about a subscription change has to say which plan, and `plan_id` is a uuid no consumer can render into words.
